title: Bees and Flowers: A Pollination Adventure

cover.title: Bees and Flowers: A Pollination Adventure
cover.subtitle: A sunny story about pollen, nectar, and seeds

pages.text: A flower is a busy place. Many plants use flowers to make seeds. Bright colors and sweet smells help bees find the blooms.
extras: Flowers can help plants make seeds.

images.alt: A honeybee resting on purple lavender flowers

pages.text: The bee dips into a flower for nectar. Nectar is sweet flower liquid. It gives the bee energy to fly, fly, fly.

images.alt: A bee searching inside a dahlia flower for nectar

pages.text: The flower also makes pollen. Pollen is a fine powder. When the bee climbs in, pollen can stick to its hairy body.
extras: Pollen can look like yellow dust.

images.alt: A bee covered with yellow pollen on a flower

pages.text: Some bees collect pollen to take home. They pack it onto special baskets on their back legs. That pollen helps feed young bees.

images.alt: A close view of a honeybee leg carrying a round yellow pollen load

pages.text: Now the bee visits another flower. Some pollen rubs off in the right place. This pollen move is called pollination.

images.alt: A simple diagram showing pollen moving between flower parts

pages.text: After pollen lands in the right spot, a flower may begin making seeds. In many flowering plants, seeds grow inside fruit.

images.alt: A bee on pink and white apple blossoms
Red and yellow apples growing on a tree after flowers became fruit

pages.text: The bee is looking for food, not trying to help on purpose. Still, bees get food from flowers, and flowers get help making seeds.
extras: Bees and flowers make a helpful team.

images.alt: A bumblebee deep inside a hibiscus flower with pollen on its body

pages.text: Pollinators help many fruits and vegetables grow. Good pollination can help plants make full, healthy fruit.

images.alt: A tomato plant with yellow flowers and small green fruits growing together

pages.text: People can help bees and flowers too. Plant many kinds of flowers that bloom at different times, and use fewer pesticides when you can.
extras: More blooms can mean more bee food.

images.alt: A small wildflower meadow planted to help bees and other pollinators
